title: A singleton fpqc covering of an affine scheme has a finite affine-open refinement
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism such that the one-member family $\{f:X\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Then there are an integer $m\ge0$, affine open subschemes $X_j\subseteq X$ for $j=1,\dots,m$, their coproduct $X'=\coprod_{j=1}^mX_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and the morphisms $h:X'\to X$ induced by the open inclusions and $g=f\circ h:X'\to S$, such that $X'$ is affine, $g$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and hence $\{g:X'\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering. The map $h$ is a morphism over $S$.

source.place: Topologies, Lemma Tag 022E (topologies-lemma-fpqc-affine, line 3151), finite affine refinement of an fpqc covering of an affine scheme, followed by the finite coproduct construction

proof.text: Apply the definition of the singleton fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] to the affine open $S\subseteq S$. It supplies $m\ge0$ and affine opens $X_1,\ldots,X_m\subseteq X$ such that $S=\bigcup_{j=1}^m f(X_j)$; also $f$ is flat. These are precisely the opens in the refinement of Topologies 022E. If $S$ is empty, $m=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering), applied to the affine open S; Lemma Tag 022E (lemma-fpqc-affine), proof 'follows directly from the definition'

proof.text: Form $X'=\coprod_{j=1}^m X_j$ and let $\iota_j:X_j\to X'$ be its coprojections. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the open inclusions $e_j:X_j\hookrightarrow X$ induce the unique map $h:X'\to X$ with $h\circ\iota_j=e_j$. Put $g=f\circ h$; thus $g\circ\iota_j=f|_{X_j}$, and $h$ is over $S$. The finite coproduct $X'$ is affine by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], including the empty coproduct $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$.

source.place: Topologies, Lemma Tag 022E (lemma-fpqc-affine), finite affine-open refinement; finite coproduct packaging of that refinement

proof.text: The image of $g$ is $\bigcup_j f(X_j)=S$, so $g$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. To check flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism], take $u\in X'$ in the $j$th component and write $x=\iota_j^{-1}(u)\in X_j$. The coprojection $\iota_j$ and the inclusion $e_j$ are open immersions [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], [def-weil-open-immersion], hence identify $\mathcal O_{X',u}$ and $\mathcal O_{X_j,x}$ with $\mathcal O_{X,e_j(x)}$. Under these identifications the local ring map for $g$ is the local ring map for $f$ at $e_j(x)$, which is flat by Step 1. Thus $g$ is flat at every point. If $X'$ is empty, flatness holds vacuously and Step 1 forces $S$ empty as well.

source.place: Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering), flatness and image condition; Lemma Tag 022E (lemma-fpqc-affine), refinement is fpqc

proof.text: It remains to verify the asserted singleton fpqc condition, including its condition over affine opens other than $S$. Since $X'$ and $S$ are affine, $g$ is an affine morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. For any affine open $U\subseteq S$, the inverse image $g^{-1}(U)$ is therefore an affine open of $X'$, and $g(g^{-1}(U))=U$ by surjectivity. This one affine open witnesses the finite-image condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] for $U$, while Step 3 supplies flatness. Hence $\{g:X'\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering.
